def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    available = bins - np.maximum(0, bins - item)
    can_fit = available >= 0
    priorities = np.zeros_like(bins)
    # Use log-based penalty: higher priority for bins where item is close to full capacity
    # Logarithmic scale penalizes large waste more heavily and favors tight fits
    # Avoid log(0) by adding epsilon; ensure ratio > 1 (since bins >= item when fitting)
    ratio = bins[can_fit] / (item + 1e-8)
    # Apply log only to ratios above 1 (i.e., bins that actually contain the item)
    # Use inverse of log(ratio) to make tighter fits (closer to 1) have higher priority
    log_penalty = np.log(ratio + 1e-8)
    # Avoid division by zero; set very small values to a large priority
    priorities[can_fit] = 1 / (log_penalty + 1e-8)
    return priorities

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining_after = bins - item
    # Mask bins that cannot fit the item
    can_fit = remaining_after >= 0
    # Initialize priorities with zeros for bins that cannot fit
    priorities = np.zeros_like(bins)
    # For bins that can fit, compute the ratio of remaining capacity to item size
    # We want to favor bins where the item takes up a large portion of the remaining space
    # This encourages more balanced usage and avoids very small leftover spaces
    ratio = np.where(remaining_after > 0, remaining_after / item, 1e-8)
    # Invert the ratio so higher values indicate better fit relative to remaining space
    priorities[can_fit] = 1 / (ratio + 1e-8)
    return priorities

    remaining = bins - item
    # Penalize bins that cannot fit the item (negative or zero remaining)
    # Use a large penalty to ensure such bins are not selected
    penalty = np.where(remaining < 0, np.inf, 0)
    # For bins that can fit the item, prioritize those with less remaining space
    # Use negative remaining space to make smaller remaining space have higher priority
    priorities = -remaining + penalty
    # Handle bins with no capacity left after adding item (set to very low priority)
    priorities = np.where(bins == 0, -np.inf, priorities)
    return priorities

    # Penalize bins that cannot fit the item
    penalty = np.where(remaining < 0, np.inf, 0)
    # Target remaining capacity is half of bin capacity
    target_remaining = bins / 2
    # Use absolute deviation from target remaining capacity
    deviation = np.abs(remaining - target_remaining)
    # Prioritize smaller deviations (closer to target), but avoid division by zero
    priorities = 1 / (deviation + 1e-8)
    # Apply penalty for bins that can't fit the item
    priorities += penalty
    # Ensure full bins have very low priority
    priorities = np.where(bins == 0, -np.inf, priorities)
    return priorities

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    current_load = bins - (bins - item).clip(min=0)
    utilization = current_load / bins
    # Favor bins with moderate utilization (not too low or too high)
    # Use a quadratic penalty around 0.5 to encourage balance
    deviation_from_optimal = np.abs(utilization - 0.5)
    priorities = 1 / (deviation_from_optimal + 1e-8)
    return priorities

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining = bins - item
    # Ensure only bins that can fit the item are considered
    valid_bins = remaining >= 0
    # Compute ideal capacity as the mean of current bin usages (excluding full bins)
    avg_usage = np.mean(bins[valid_bins]) if np.any(valid_bins) else 0
    ideal_capacity = avg_usage + item
    # Compute deviation of each bin's remaining capacity from ideal
    deviation = np.abs(remaining - ideal_capacity)
    # Normalize deviation to prioritize bins closest to ideal
    max_deviation = np.max(deviation) if np.any(deviation > 0) else 1
    normalized_deviation = deviation / max_deviation
    # Assign higher priority to bins with smaller deviation (closer to ideal)
    priorities = -normalized_deviation
    # Penalize invalid bins (cannot fit item) with very low priority
    priorities = np.where(~valid_bins, -np.inf, priorities)
    return priorities
